title: 362. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Area of Composite Figures
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Area of a Rectangle and an Attached Square
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the total area of two non-overlapping shapes by addition.
questions.question: A rectangle measures \(8\text{ cm}\) by \(5\text{ cm}\). A square with side length \(3\text{ cm}\) is attached outside the rectangle along part of one side, without overlap. What is the total area?
questions.explanation: The rectangle has area \(8\times5=40\text{ cm}^2\). The square has area \(3\times3=9\text{ cm}^2\). Since the shapes do not overlap, their total area is \(40+9=49\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: Find the area of each part before combining the two areas.

questions.learningObjective: Determine a remaining area by subtracting a rectangular cutout from a larger rectangle.
questions.question: A rectangular courtyard measures \(12\text{ m}\) by \(7\text{ m}\). A \(4\text{ m}\) by \(3\text{ m}\) rectangular section is removed from one corner. What is the remaining area?
questions.explanation: The original courtyard has area \(12\times7=84\text{ m}^2\). The removed rectangle has area \(4\times3=12\text{ m}^2\). Subtracting gives \(84-12=72\text{ m}^2\).
questions.hint: Calculate the area of the original rectangle, then subtract the missing part.

questions.concept: Adding a Triangle to a Rectangle
questions.learningObjective: Apply the triangle area formula when finding a composite area.
questions.question: A rectangle measures \(10\text{ cm}\) by \(6\text{ cm}\). A triangle is attached externally along the rectangle's \(10\text{ cm}\) side, without overlap. The triangle has base \(10\text{ cm}\) and perpendicular height \(4\text{ cm}\). What is the composite area?
questions.explanation: The rectangle contributes \(10\times6=60\text{ cm}^2\). The triangle contributes \(\frac{1}{2}\times10\times4=20\text{ cm}^2\), not \(40\text{ cm}^2\). Therefore, the composite area is \(60+20=80\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: Use half the product of the triangle's base and perpendicular height.

questions.learningObjective: Find the area of an L-shaped region formed by two overlapping rectangular strips.
questions.question: An L-shaped region is the union of a horizontal \(10\text{ m}\) by \(4\text{ m}\) strip and a vertical \(3\text{ m}\) by \(8\text{ m}\) strip. Their overlap is exactly a \(3\text{ m}\) by \(4\text{ m}\) rectangle. What is the area of the L-shaped region?
questions.explanation: Adding the strip areas gives \(10\times4+3\times8=64\text{ m}^2\), but the overlap is counted twice. Subtract its area once: \(64-3\times4=52\text{ m}^2\).
questions.hint: When adding the two strip areas, check whether any region is counted more than once.

questions.concept: Area of a Rectangle with an Attached Semicircle
questions.learningObjective: Calculate a composite area using the radius derived from a semicircle's diameter.
questions.question: A \(10\text{ cm}\) by \(6\text{ cm}\) rectangle has a semicircle attached externally along one \(6\text{ cm}\) side, without overlap. The semicircle's diameter is \(6\text{ cm}\). What is the exact total area?
questions.explanation: The rectangle has area \(10\times6=60\text{ cm}^2\). The semicircle's radius is \(3\text{ cm}\), so its area is \(\frac{1}{2}\pi(3)^2=\frac{9\pi}{2}\text{ cm}^2\). Add the parts to obtain \(\left(60+\frac{9\pi}{2}\right)\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: Convert the semicircle's diameter to its radius and remember that it is half of a circle.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the area of a U-shaped figure by subtracting a rectangular notch.
questions.question: A U-shaped region is made from an \(18\text{ m}\) by \(12\text{ m}\) rectangle by removing a notch \(8\text{ m}\) wide and \(7\text{ m}\) deep from the middle of one \(18\text{ m}\) side. What area remains?
questions.explanation: The outer rectangle has area \(18\times12=216\text{ m}^2\). The notch reaches only \(7\text{ m}\) into the shape, so its area is \(8\times7=56\text{ m}^2\). The remaining area is \(216-56=160\text{ m}^2\).
questions.hint: Use the notch depth rather than the full outer height when finding the area to subtract.

questions.concept: Combining an Area Cutout and an Added Triangle
questions.learningObjective: Find a composite area involving both subtraction and triangle-area addition.
questions.question: A figure starts as a \(15\text{ cm}\) by \(9\text{ cm}\) rectangle. A \(6\text{ cm}\) by \(5\text{ cm}\) rectangle is removed from one corner. A triangle with base \(5\text{ cm}\) and perpendicular height \(4\text{ cm}\) is then attached outside an uncut side, without overlap. What is the final area?
questions.explanation: Start with \(15\times9=135\text{ cm}^2\), then subtract the corner cutout, \(6\times5=30\text{ cm}^2\). Add the triangle area, \(\frac{1}{2}\times5\times4=10\text{ cm}^2\). The result is \(135-30+10=115\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: Treat the removed rectangle as a subtraction and the new triangle as an addition.

questions.concept: Subtracting a Square Hole from a Trapezoid
questions.learningObjective: Apply the trapezoid area formula and subtract the area of an interior square hole.
questions.question: A trapezoidal sheet has parallel sides of length \(14\text{ cm}\) and \(8\text{ cm}\), with perpendicular height \(5\text{ cm}\). A \(4\text{ cm}\) by \(4\text{ cm}\) square hole is cut entirely from its interior. What is the area of the remaining sheet?
questions.explanation: The trapezoid area is \(\frac{14+8}{2}\times5=55\text{ cm}^2\). The square hole has area \(4\times4=16\text{ cm}^2\). Subtracting gives \(55-16=39\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: First use the average of the parallel sides to find the trapezoid area.

questions.concept: Finding an Unknown Notch Depth from Composite Area
questions.learningObjective: Determine a missing linear dimension using the original area and the remaining composite area.
questions.question: An L-shaped patio is formed by removing a rectangular corner notch \(3\text{ m}\) wide and \(d\text{ m}\) deep from an \(11\text{ m}\) by \(7\text{ m}\) rectangle. The remaining area is \(59\text{ m}^2\). What is \(d\)?
questions.explanation: The original rectangle has area \(11\times7=77\text{ m}^2\). The removed notch therefore has area \(77-59=18\text{ m}^2\). Since its width is \(3\text{ m}\), its depth is \(d=\frac{18}{3}=6\text{ m}\), which fits within the original \(7\text{ m}\) height.
questions.hint: Find the missing area first, then use the notch width to determine its depth.

questions.concept: Combining a Semicircular Extension and an Interior Cutout
questions.learningObjective: Synthesize rectangular area, an interior subtraction, and an external semicircular addition.
questions.question: A rectangular park measures \(20\text{ m}\) by \(12\text{ m}\). A \(6\text{ m}\) by \(4\text{ m}\) pond lies entirely inside the park and is excluded from its land area. A semicircular lawn of diameter \(12\text{ m}\) is attached externally along a \(12\text{ m}\) side of the park, without overlap. What is the exact total land area, including the lawn but excluding the pond?
questions.explanation: The rectangular park contributes \(20\times12=240\text{ m}^2\). Exclude the pond area \(6\times4=24\text{ m}^2\). The semicircle has radius \(6\text{ m}\), so its area is \(\frac{1}{2}\pi(6)^2=18\pi\text{ m}^2\). The required total is \(240-24+18\pi=216+18\pi\text{ m}^2\).
questions.hint: Account separately for the main rectangle, the interior region that does not count, and the external semicircle.
